evidence:
Authored for this product: every task file is HireOps-specific. instruction.md:1 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?'; task.toml [task] name 'turing/hireops-recruiting-operations', arena_slice 'recruiting-hiring-operations', provenance 'Adapted from the supplied HireOps task as a recruiting workspace, with an authored reference implementation and browser rubric.' All template CHANGE_ME placeholders (template instruction.md:1, task.toml name/description/arena_slice/provenance, app_context.md Name/Accounts/Key screens) are replaced with product content. A grep of the frozen task (excluding node_modules) for sibling product nouns (bazaar|torque|colder|docket|pellmoor|threadline|ridgeline|patchpad|gridforge|coursemark|orbital|medcare|expense|utilibill|drawbill|oriel|boardloom|CHANGE_ME|vacanc|merchant|channel) found only hireops_rules.md:12 'nothing a request claims' (ordinary verb) and solution/app/public/js/app.js:139 BroadcastChannel('hireops-live') (browser API) - no carried-over sibling entities. Criteria ids are product-prefixed (hro_*, 43 functional) and the functional/polish/visual prompts name HireOps roles, Noor Haddad's 120-message Platform Engineer conversation and HireOps screens.
Sibling comparison (row's Defect: same flows, same criteria, renamed entities): the only same-domain sibling is projects/pellmoor-job-pipeline (arena_slice full-stack-typescript-d3-esbuild-express-sqlite-pipeline). Shared generic recruiting concepts exist - no stage skipping (Pellmoor hiring-rules.md 'Do not skip stages' vs hireops_rules.md:47 'one stage at a time'), a capacity limit (vacancy offer capacity vs Interview places hireops_rules.md:61-65), and atomic batches (Pellmoor 'atomic batch offers' vs hireops_rules.md:87-92). But the flows and criteria differ materially: Pellmoor centres on interview panels, 1-5 scoring, assessment-version freshness, a d3 funnel derived from stage history, append-only notes and idempotent receipts, with only the hiring manager moving candidates and one-step backsteps; HireOps centres on recruiter/hiring-manager/observer/candidate roles, hand-ordered cards within a stage shared by everyone, stale-card 409 with 'who moved it', optimistic move with put-back and focus retention, bulk move + single-level undo invalidated by later touches, 15-second live updates that preserve focus/draft/scroll/open card, recruiter-candidate conversations with 30-message paging that keeps the reader's place, per-person unread and 'seen' marks, per-user per-browser drafts surviving session expiry, and a candidate portal with candidate wording and staff-data redaction. Criterion id sets share no ids or structure (Pellmoor: authentication_sessions_and_revocation, exact_derived_funnel, offer_requires_a_complete_independent_panel, panel_change_invalidates_entire_assessment, successful_retry_replays_one_result...; HireOps: hro_live_board, hro_thread_earlier, hro_unread_scrolled_up, hro_seen, hro_drafts, hro_candidate_private, hro_undo_conflict...). Threadline-chat shares only the generic 'load older messages without disturbing position' / per-user unread idea; it is a team chat with channels, threads, reactions, pins, webhooks and presence, not a staff-candidate conversation on an application. Neither sibling is a nouns-swapped source for HireOps.
Domain plan: no suite domain-plan document exists in the workspace (searched for 'Deliverables Tracker'/'domain plan' outside qc/runs; only workbook inventories matched). Fit is judged from the arena_slice taxonomy across projects/*/task.toml: HireOps occupies a distinct slice ('recruiting-hiring-operations') and a distinct product angle (real-time multi-user pipeline + candidate messaging) from Pellmoor (TS/d3 assessment funnel). The product was supplied by the user (provenance), so the domain choice is user-directed.
Adversarial check: this row grades task identity, not app behaviour, so 'broken app that could pass / conforming app that could fail' does not apply directly; the analogous attempt - finding a sibling whose flows/criteria map one-to-one onto HireOps after renaming - failed for every sibling examined. Observation (not a defect): HireOps and Pellmoor are two recruiting-domain tasks in one portfolio; if the lead's suite plan caps one task per domain, that is a portfolio decision outside this task's files.
